title: A join is a lookup with a contract

blocks.text: A purchase table can contain many purchases from the same store. A store lookup table should contain one rate per store. Joining these tables enriches purchases with rates. It does not combine purchases into totals, and it does not compare row numbers. A purchase with key B must find the right-side B even if B appears at another row position.
Join DataFrames on keys. Require unique right-side keys, allowing many left rows per right row. Preserve left order for a left join.

A key is a value used to match rows. A left join keeps every left row. Cardinality describes how many matches one row can have. Many-to-one means repeated keys are permitted on the left but must be unique on the right.

Follow the two B purchases in the animation. Both use the same lookup value 20 and remain separate rows. The unmatched C purchase is still present because this is a left join; its rate is missing. The question additionally asks to preserve left order, so the B,A,B,C sequence matters. The example checks that sequence instead of assuming a sorted output is equivalent.

blocks.text: Connect the picture to the mathematics

blocks.caption: kᴸ and kᴿ are left and right keys. The right-side uniqueness constraint makes the count at most one for each matched left row.

blocks.text: Turn on the duplicate-key scenario. If B appears twice on the right, each left B purchase has two matches. A normal many-to-many merge would create two copies of each B purchase. This can silently inflate totals downstream. The supplied validate="many_to_one" raises an error instead, because ambiguity in the lookup violates this task’s stated contract.

Do not repair duplicate lookup keys by dropping an arbitrary row without deciding what the duplicates mean. They might indicate versions that need an effective-date rule, conflicting records, or a missing join key. A correct implementation should join on all required key columns. After joining, check row count, key order, unmatched values, and whether duplicate right keys are rejected. These tests catch different failure modes.

checks.prompt: Two left B rows match one right B row. How many B rows are in the result?

explanation.correct: Each left row has one right match, so the two rows stay distinct.
